item.title: Sympathetic Cooling of Ionic Fullerenes with Ultracold Atoms to Millikelvin Temperatures
item.description: arXiv:2611.05815v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cooling complex molecular ions to millikelvin temperatures remains a major challenge because their intricate internal structures prevent laser cooling. Here, we propose to use an ultracold gas of Cd atoms to efficiently cool C$_{60}^+$ ions to average kinetic energies of approximately 20 mK, following an initial precooling stage with He buffer gas. Our approach is based on full molecular dynamics simulations using accurate ion-atom interaction potentials derived from high-level electronic structure methods. Furthermore, using a Monte Carlo approach, we predict the formation of C$_{60}^+$ Coulomb crystals supported solely by collisions with the buffer gas. The probability of reaching these cold states shows a pronounced dependence on the number of trapped ions, revealing the competition between neutral-atom cooling and many-ion dynamics in radio-frequency traps.
item.dc:creator: Saajid Chowdhury, Zhongqi Liang, Yu Wang, Jes\'us P\'erez-R\'ios

item.title: The two-loop Lamb shift: the final missing contribution
item.description: arXiv:2611.05978v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The last significant unknown contribution to the two-loop Lamb shift, namely the electron self-energy with vacuum-polarization insertion into the photon line, is determined including higher-order effects in the parameter $\alpha Z$, with $\alpha$ being the fine-structure constant and $Z$ the nuclear charge number. Our calculation improves the accuracy of theoretical predictions for energy levels and transition energies in heavy hydrogen-like and lithium-like ions by up to one order of magnitude, enabling more stringent comparisons between theory and available experimental results. These results pave the way for more precise tests of quantum electrodynamics in the strong-field regime, as well as for accurate determinations of nuclear charge radii.
item.dc:creator: J. Sommerfeldt, V. A. Yerokhin, Z. Harman, C. H. Keitel

item.title: Nuclear recoil with electron vacuum polarization in muonic atoms
item.description: arXiv:2611.06480v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Using the heavy-particle QED approach, we derive the last missing $\alpha\,(Z\alpha)^5\,m^2/M$ nuclear recoil correction in muonic atoms, which originates from the combination of the $(Z\alpha)^5\,m^2/M$ recoil with the electron vacuum polarization. Numerical results are presented for the $1S$, $2S$, and $2P$ states of $\mu$H, $\mu$D, $\mu^3$He$^+$, and $\mu^4$He$^+$. For the $2P-2S$ Lamb shift in muonic helium ions, our results are of opposite sign and about four times smaller in magnitude than the previous logarithmic estimates.
item.dc:creator: Vojt\v{e}ch Patk\'o\v{s}, Mateusz Pa\'{n}tak, Krzysztof Pachucki

item.title: Cryogenic suppression of correlated loss in Rydberg atom arrays
item.description: arXiv:2611.06613v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Blackbody radiation (BBR) poses a central challenge for quantum science with Rydberg atoms. By driving transitions to nearby opposite-parity states, BBR shortens Rydberg lifetimes and has long been suspected to trigger "avalanche" events known to cause correlated atom loss. Here, we suppress avalanche decay and establish BBR as its dominant trigger using a Rydberg atom array that operates either cryogenically or at room temperature. A $45~\text{K}$ radiation shield reduces ambient BBR, extending Rydberg $nS$ lifetimes for $n$ ranging from 50 to 75. BBR-induced decay rates are suppressed by 30%-50%, corresponding to an effective blackbody temperature $T_{\rm eff}\approx190~\text{K}$. This enables controlled comparisons of Rydberg-dressed atom arrays operating in different BBR environments. Arrays of up to 70 atoms demonstrate cryogenically suppressed avalanche rates, tracking the suppression in BBR-induced decay, for both $n=50$ and $n=60$ dressing. A parameter-free rate model agrees with the measured avalanche rates after accounting for frequency-dependent cryogenic shielding, photoionization-triggered avalanches, laser phase noise, BBR decay channels, and Rydberg interaction effects. We demonstrate a quantitative description of avalanche decay and show that improved BBR shielding should further suppress correlated loss to the $T_\text{eff}=45~\text{K}$ achievable in the current apparatus. Our results establish a route to mitigating correlated errors that otherwise impede fault-tolerant operation in neutral-atom quantum processors.
item.dc:creator: Zhenpu Zhang, Brendan P. Marsh, Ting You Tan, Quinn Manning, Daniel H. Slichter, Adam M. Kaufman, Cindy A. Regal

item.title: Search for the 229Pa Parity Doublet via Internal-Conversion Spectroscopy at FRIB
item.description: arXiv:2611.05494v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The radioisotope $^{229}$Pa is predicted to possess a nearly degenerate ground-state parity doublet. Previous $\gamma$-ray and conversion-electron spectroscopy suggests a splitting of $\Delta E = (60\pm 50)~\mathrm{eV}$, although the doublet's existence remains unconfirmed. Such a small splitting would give $^{229}$Pa an exceptionally large enhancement of symmetry-violating nuclear properties. However, the splitting, and with it the sensitivity of $^{229}$Pa to CP-violating physics, remains uncertain by orders of magnitude. We propose an experiment to measure this splitting with sub-eV precision within a few days of measurement time by using delayed-coincidence internal-conversion spectroscopy of $^{229}$Pa ions produced by the electron-capture decay of $^{229}$U$^{+}$ ions stored in a Penning trap at the Facility for Rare Isotope Beams (FRIB). This measurement would provide the key nuclear-structure input needed to establish $^{229}$Pa as a leading candidate for next-generation atomic and molecular electric-dipole-moment (EDM) experiments.
item.dc:creator: Silviu-Marian Udrescu, Aiden Boyer, Lan Cheng, Ronald Fernando Garcia Ruiz, Phay J. Ho, Ryan Ringle, Jaideep T. Singh, Patrick R. Stollenwerk, Georg Tiebel, Margaret J. Tseng

item.title: Collectively pumped superradiant laser with coherence scaling beyond the standard quantum limit
item.description: arXiv:2611.05976v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For more than half a century, the standard quantum limit (SQL) was thought to limit the laser coherence $\mathfrak{C}$ -- the number of photons emitted from the laser into the beam in one coherence time -- to a scaling $\Theta(\mu^2)$, where $\mu$ is the mean number of optical-frequency excitations stored inside the laser. However, recently it has been shown [Baker et al., Nat. Phys. 17, 179 (2021)] that the Heisenberg limit -- an achievable ultimate limit set by quantum mechanics for the task of producing a beam with the standard properties of a laser beam -- is $\mathfrak{C}=\Theta(\mu^4)$, a quadratic enhancement. So far, proposals to demonstrate beyond-SQL scaling of $\mathfrak{C}$ have been limited to circuit QED, at microwave frequencies (i.e., a maser). Here, we introduce a class of generalized far-above-threshold (FAT) laser models, obtained by replacing the ordinary bosonic lowering operator $\hat{a}$ by a general lowering operator $\hat{L}$ in the superoperators appearing in the master equation that governs the FAT laser dynamics. We then show that an optical-frequency superradiant laser in the bad-cavity limit, with feedback-controlled collective pumping, realizes one such model, in which $\hat{L}$ is identified with the collective superradiant lowering operator $\hat{J}$. This model can surpass the SQL scaling, with the coherence exhibiting a scaling as large as $\mathfrak{C}= \Theta(\mu^{8/3})$ in the optimal parameter regime. Here, in the bad-cavity limit, $\mu\approx N/2$, where $N$ is the number of superradiant atoms.
item.dc:creator: Ori Somech, Howard M. Wiseman

item.title: Photoionization rates of oxygen and nitrogen at 800 nm measured by Thomson coherent microwave scattering
item.description: arXiv:2611.06729v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this study, we report on the use of Thomson coherent microwave scattering (CMS) to characterize photoionization rates in oxygen and nitrogen at 800 nm over a range spanning approximately three orders of magnitude, from about mid-10$^9$ s$^{-1}$ range to the to mid-10$^{12}$ s$^{-1}$ range, corresponding to laser intensities in the vicinity of 10$^{13}$-10$^{14}$ W/cm$^2$, a range of significant practical relevance to filamentation physics.
item.dc:creator: K. Reindersma, M. Malaussena, S. Anantaram, K. Patel, V. Kumar, N. Babusis, M. Slipchenko, A. Shashurin

item.title: Absolute frequency measurement of the $^{40}$Ca$^{+}$ clock transition using a GNSS link to the SI second
item.description: arXiv:2609.15844v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We report the absolute frequency measurement of the $4s$ $ ^{2}S_{1/2}\leftrightarrow 3d$ $^{2}D_{5/2}$ $^{40}$Ca$^{+}$ clock transition with respect to the SI second. To perform this measurement, a link between our laboratory in Innsbruck and the clocks realizing the Coordinated Universal Time at the Physikalisch-Technische Bundesanstalt (PTB) in Braunschweig was installed and characterized using the Global Navigation Satellite System GNSS. The comparison between our clock and the ones at PTB was done using the Precise Point Positioning technique. After the evaluation of the systematic shifts, the measured transition frequency is 411 042 129 776 400.4$\pm$0.6 Hz with a fractional uncertainty of 1.5 $\times$ 10$^{-15}$. The stability of the clock measurements was also corroborated by comparing two different calcium ion clock experiments, which share the clock laser source at our institute. Furthermore, after careful evaluation of the trap-drive induced ac magnetic fields, we estimate ac Zeeman shifts on the $D_{5/2}$ sublevels and reevaluate the Land\'e g-factor of the $3d$ $^{2}D_{5/2}$ level to be g$_{5/2}= 1.200329(1)$.
item.dc:creator: M. Guevara-Bertsch, M. K. Joshi, M. I Hussain, R. Blatt, C. F. Roos

item.title: Stability and mixed phases of three-component droplets in one dimension
item.description: arXiv:2601.04950v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We explore the ground state properties and excitation spectra of one-dimensional, three-component bosonic mixtures, where two majority components form a self-bound droplet coupled to a third, minority component. Within a self-consistent Lee-Huang-Yang framework, we identify distinct mixed self-bound droplet phases and characterize their phase transitions through variations of either the particle number of the majority components or the intercomponent coupling. The ensuing phases demonstrate that the minority component is untrapped, partially trapped, or fully trapped by the majority droplet species. These states are characterized by their binding energies captured by the chemical potentials and their low-amplitude excitation spectrum, including mode crossings at the particle-emission threshold. We further derive effective reduced models in the high-imbalance limit, which accurately reproduce the numerically computed ground states, while providing analytical insights into the role of quantum fluctuations. Our results establish the stability and structure of mixed droplet phases provide experimentally relevant signatures for their identification.
item.dc:creator: I. A. Englezos, E. G. Charalampidis, P. Schmelcher, S. I. Mistakidis

item.title: Bidirectional teleportation using scrambling dynamics: a practical protocol
item.description: arXiv:2601.15536v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that quantum information scrambling can enable a generic SWAP gate between collective degrees of freedom in systems without universal local control. Our protocol combines a Hayden-Preskill type recovery scheme, associated with the black hole information paradox, with quantum teleportation and runs them in parallel and in opposite directions, enabling bidirectional exchange of quantum states through global interactions alone. This approach cleanly distinguishes the roles of information spreading, entanglement, and chaos for enabling both coherent state transfer and recovery. We propose an experimental realization using the Dicke model, which can be realized in optical cavity and trapped-ion platforms, highlighting the utility of holography in designing practical quantum gates.
item.dc:creator: Amit Vikram, Edwin Chaparro, Muhammad Miskeen Khan, Andrew Lucas, Chris Akers, Ana Maria Rey

item.title: Pump-scheme dependence of few-emitter lasers: exact multilevel correlations and photon statistics
item.description: arXiv:2611.01205v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Few-emitter laser models usually replace the excitation cycle of the gain medium by a single Markovian pump jump of a two-level emitter. We test this replacement with the cavity and laser-transition parameters held fixed and the two-level pump rate fitted to the same mean photon number, using an exact damping-basis continued-fraction solution of the cavity--emitter master equation for $N$ identical $d$-level emitters with arbitrary independent incoherent transitions and one cavity-coupled transition, in the known reduced space of level populations and lasing coherences. First, a pump-quantum filtration shows that the inter-emitter coherence of $\Lambda$ and ladder media starts at second rather than first order in the pump; we evaluate its leading coefficient from the exact finite-system series and map the recycling rate at which its sign changes. Second, at matched photon number, rate-limited steps in the pump cycle push the long-time output-counting Fano factor of two and three emitters well below one: for two emitters it reaches 0.66 at a mean cavity occupation of 0.3 and is still 0.74 at an occupation of one, where $g^{(2)}(0)$ is within 3% of unity, because the anticorrelation sits at delays of about half a cavity lifetime rather than at zero delay. For two and three emitters the fitted two-level model gets both statistics wrong and places the output above the shot-noise level. Against independent single-emitter lasers at the same output, the common cavity erodes rather than enhances this single-emitter effect.
item.dc:creator: Stephan Hartmann
